Petitioner / accused No.1 has preferred this petition under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. praying to enlarge him on bail in crime No.49/2023 of Davanagere Women Police Station registered for the offence punishable under Sections 506, 498A, 504, 307, 323, 324 and 114 of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2. FIR is registered on the basis of a complaint lodged by the victim, wife of the petitioner against accused Nos.1 to 5.

Charge sheet is filed for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 504, 323,
324, 506, 114, 326, 307 read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.
3.
The learned counsel for petitioner submits that the marriage between the petitioner and the complainant was a love marriage and due to some matrimonial dispute, the present complaint has been filed.
He submits that the victim is already discharged from the hospital and there is no life threat to her.
He submits that the petitioner is NC: 2023:KHC:45189 eking out his livelihood by doing coolie work and therefore, if he is not released on bail, his entire family members will suffer.
He further submits that accused Nos.2 to 5 are already enlarged on bail and on similar conditions the petitioner may also be released on bail.
4. The learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the prayer contending that if the petitioner is enlarged on bail there is life threat to the victim.
She has drawn the attention of the Court to the nature of injuries sustained by the victim.
She contends that the victim has been assaulted by the petitioner with an iron rod indiscriminately and he has attempted to kill her.
She contends that if the petitioner is released on bail, he may try to influence or threaten her and therefore, sought to reject the petition.
5. During crime stage, the petitioner had preferred Crl.P.5187/2023 which was dismissed reserving liberty to him to file a fresh petition before the Sessions Court after completion of investigation.

After the charge sheet was NC: 2023:KHC:45189 filed the learned Sessions Judge has rejected the petition filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
6.

The complaint averments reveal that the marriage of the petitioner with the complainant was a love marriage and the marriage was registered in the Office of the Sub registrar, Hirekeroor on 06.07.2021.
For about 6 months the couple were in a cordial relationship.
Subsequently, the petitioner and his family members started to harass the victim, for the purpose of dowry.

sentences.text:
It is stated that the petitioner was giving physical and mental torture to the complainant,
suspecting her character and demanding her to bring money from her parental home.
Even when she was pregnant, he did not stop the torture.
On the other hand, he was abusing and assaulting her.
On 09.05.2023 at about 05:30 pm, he assaulted her with an iron rod indiscriminately all over her body, on account of which she sustained grievous injuries.

8. The wound certificate made available by the learned High Court Government Pleader shows that the NC: 2023:KHC:45189 victim sustained several injuries, out of which injury numbers 3 to 5 are stated to be grievous in nature.
She has suffered fracture in post aspect of 10th rib on left side and disarticulation of 5th Metacarpo-Phalangeal joint of right hand and left hand Ap/oblique -fracture in left ulnar styloid process.
9. The nature of injuries suffered by the victim shows that she has been assaulted mercilessly all over her body.
Victim is the wife of the petitioner.
He was supposed to take care of her, instead he was subjecting her to torture suspecting her character.
10. There is a prima facie case against the petitioner.
Apart from the victim, there are two other eye witnesses who are cited as CW-3 and 5 in the charge sheet.
The grounds urged by the learned counsel for petitioner cannot be considered at this stage to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

As rightly contended by the learned High Court Government Pleader in the event of release of the petitioner,
he may threaten or influence the victim, who is NC: 2023:KHC:45189 his wife and therefore this is not a fit case to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
11. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.

Sd/-
